requires.label: Colorado residency required
requires.quote: An individual must be a Resident of Colorado in order to qualify for Financial Assistance.

rules.label: Catastrophic Balance Financial Assistance
rules.quote: The Patient's outstanding single account balance due after all insurance or third-party payments and/or discounts (including the application of Financial Assistance based on family income alone) is greater than 50% of the Patient's total annual Family Income and Financial Resources combined.

rules.label: Presumptive Eligibility for Financial Assistance
rules.quote: Presumptive eligibility for Financial Assistance may be granted for circumstances outlined in the Presumptive Eligibility section of this policy.

application.quote: Applicants have the later of (a) 365 days from the date of the first post-discharge Billing Statement, or (b) 30 days after notice of the initiation of one or more Extraordinary Collection Actions ("ECA") has been provided, to submit an application or to request a reconsideration of an incomplete and denied application

eca_not_before.quote: UCHealth does not initiate ECAs prior to (a) 365 days from the date UCHealth provides the first post-discharge Billing Statement to the Patient; and (b) reasonable efforts have been made to determine whether a Guarantor is approved for Financial Assistance under this policy, as described in this section.

notes: For patients being screened for HDC, UCHealth does not deny discounted care on the basis the patient has not applied for any public benefits program or deny an admission or treatment because the patient may qualify for discounted care.

UCHealth employees residing outside the State of Colorado, but who receive services at a UCHealth facility do not have to meet residency requirements for financial assistance applications they may request.
For unscheduled emergency services, UCHealth may, at its sole discretion, make an exception to the residency requirement.
If Family Income is at or below 250% of FPL, Financial Assistance is valid for 365 days from the date of the last signed and dated Financial Assistance Application.
If Family Income is between 251-400% of FPL, eligibility for Financial Assistance is valid for 180 days from the date of the last signed and dated Financial Assistance Application.

UCHealth will not charge Patients approved for Financial Assistance more than the amount generally billed (AGB) by UCHealth to insured Patients for emergency or Medically Necessary care covered by this policy.
If the self-pay discount for a hospital facility is greater than AGB, a discount equal to the self-pay discount will be applied to gross charges to a Patient approved for Financial Assistance.

Patients approved for Catastrophic Balance Financial Assistance will receive a discount on gross charges as outlined in Appendix A or 50% of their total annual Family Income, whichever results in the lesser outstanding balance due.
The Catastrophic Balance discount mirrors the discount for those with annual Family Income between 351% and 400% of FPL guidelines.
Information from the predictive model may be used to determine presumptive eligibility for Financial Assistance when the estimated household FPL is reported to be 250% or less.
Presumptive eligibility for Financial Assistance will only apply to current services and past accounts. Presumptive eligibility does not extend to future services.
UCHealth will process completed applications within 14 days of UCHealth's receipt, and will provide a written notice of determination to the applicant.

UCHealth will send at least four (4) monthly Billing Statements, mailed every thirty (30) days, to the Guarantor of an account informing of a balance due with an address in the United States, Canada or Mexico.
After UCHealth has sent four (4) Billing Statements and received no payment and no application within thirty days of the final Billing Statement, UCHealth may refer the account to collections.
UCHealth will refer accounts to collections when insured Patient balances have not been paid for 120 days or more.
UCHealth will refer accounts to collections when uninsured Patient balances have not been paid for 182 days or more.

If no action is taken by the Guarantor to resolve the balance 365 days from the first post-discharge Billing Statement to the Patient, either by making a payment, submitting additional information or a completed application, or setting up a payment plan, the collections agency may initiate ECAs, such as initiating legal action and wage garnishment.

UCHealth will refrain from initiating ECAs for at least 365 days from the date the Hospital mails the first post-discharge Billing Statement to the Guarantor for the care, and will make reasonable efforts as described above and as required by law, at least 30 days in advance of initiating ECAs, to determine if the Patient is eligible for Financial Assistance.
All parties engaged in collection actions on behalf of UCHealth will be required to follow this policy, including contracted collection agencies.
Patient debt with UCHealth is not reported to credit agencies nor are liens placed on the patient's property.

The UCHealth Financial Counseling department will have final authority to decide whether UCHealth has made reasonable efforts to determine whether a Patient is eligible for Financial Assistance under this policy, and therefore whether UCHealth may engage in ECAs against the Guarantor.
